analysis: Production change is only in LifecycleMailbox.swift read(at:) (head line 81): adds O_NONBLOCK to open(). Before, a same-UID process could place a FIFO at a mailbox path (e.g. <pid>-<start>.addon-request.json, switch-request, or a claimed rename target) and an open(O_RDONLY) with no writer would block the reader (provider loop/monitor or CLI) indefinitely, a local DoS (T-059 class / A-018 availability). With O_NONBLOCK, open on a FIFO returns immediately, and the following fstat check (S_IFREG, uid, mode 0o077==0, size<=8192) rejects it. O_NOFOLLOW, ownership and permission checks remain; the directory lstat check in claim() and write() is unchanged. After the open the nonblocking flag stays on the descriptor, but since only regular files pass the fstat guard, FileHandle.read on a regular file is unaffected. This is a hardening with no regression identified. Residual: rename() in claim() of a FIFO still moves it and the deferred removeItem unlinks it; that is fine. Claim does not verify the source type before rename, but read() rejects it afterward. The AddonHoldStore.read FIFO test (AddonHoldStoreTests.swift ~98-106) asserts non-blocking refusal, but the AddonHoldStore implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so whether it uses O_NONBLOCK as well cannot be confirmed here. Other changes are tests only: AddonHoldLoadFenceTests (load in flight at hold start never publishes; hold stays draining until load ends, then held; no resident models), AddonHoldLoopTests (straggler cancellation spares work accepted after release, and the preload plan is not rewritten while held), and a FIFO helper. They exercise controls in ProviderLoop addon-hold code (addonHoldSettleTimeout, addonHoldBeforeCancellingStragglersForTesting) that is not supplied here, so those source changes, which implement the T-059/A-018 load fence, should be reviewed in their own batch. Test code has no production attack surface.
